t: This is Grosvenor Square, a large garden square in Mayfair. It's the centrepiece of the Duke of Westminster's Mayfair property and takes its name from his family name, Grosvenor. It was developed for fashionable homes in the 18th century. In the 20th century it had an American and Canadian diplomatic presence, and today it's mixed use and commercial. Several notable people lived or died around the square. The general Charles Cornwallis, who surrendered at Yorktown, was born here. John Stuart, Earl of Bute, the prime minister from 1762 to 1763, died here. So did Charles Canning, the first Viceroy of India.
